name: Fort Frederica National Monument
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Fort Frederica National Monument on St. Simons Island, Georgia, preserves the archaeological remains of a fortified town founded in 1736 by James Edward Oglethorpe as the southern outpost of the British colony of Georgia. The settlement served as a military buffer between British Georgia and Spanish Florida during a period of intense colonial rivalry. In 1742, British troops from Frederica defeated a larger Spanish invasion force at the nearby Battle of Bloody Marsh — a decisive engagement that effectively ended Spain's attempts to reclaim Georgia. At its peak, Frederica was home to about 500 soldiers and civilians. The monument was established in 1936 to preserve the town's ruins and earthwork fortifications.
